meta.grade_target: Stabilize NCERT Class 9 → bridge to Class 10
meta.source_textbook: NCERT Class 9 Mathematics, Chapter 1: Number Systems
meta.pedagogy: Number Sense and Fluency — visual manipulatives, decomposition, why-before-how

days.title: Integers on the Number Line
days.core_concept: Directed distance from zero; positive right, negative left
days.ncert_reference: Section 1.1 — Number line representation of integers (foundation for Ex 1.1)

ncert_problem.statement: Represent −3 and 2 on the same number line. Which integer is farther from zero?
steps: Drag a marker to −3 on the number line

days.title: Adding and Subtracting Integers
days.core_concept: Subtracting a negative equals adding a positive
days.ncert_reference: Prerequisite arithmetic for Section 1.1 rational operations

steps: Place −5 on the number line (starting point)
Move 3 units in the positive direction from −5

days.title: Rational Numbers on the Number Line
days.core_concept: Fractions as points between integers; sign determines side of zero
days.ncert_reference: NCERT Ex 1.1 Q1 — Locate 5/2 on the number line (Example 1 style)

steps: Mark the halfway point between 2 and 3

days.title: Adding Fractions — Common Denominator
days.core_concept: Equivalent fractions via LCD before adding numerators
days.ncert_reference: NCERT Section 1.1 — addition of rational numbers (7/8 + 5/9 style)

ncert_problem.statement: Find 1/3 + 1/4 using an area model, then compute symbolically.
steps: Shade 1/3 of a unit square in the grid
Shade 1/4 of the same unit (different color overlay)

days.title: Subtracting Fractions
days.core_concept: Subtraction as missing addend; common denominator first
days.ncert_reference: NCERT Section 1.1 — subtraction of rational numbers

days.title: Multiplying Fractions — Area Model
days.ncert_reference: NCERT Section 1.1 — multiplication of rational numbers

ncert_problem.statement: Find 2/3 × 3/5 using a rectangular area model.
steps: Divide grid into 3 rows; shade 2 rows (2/3)
Divide grid into 5 columns; shade 3 columns (3/5)
Count overlapping shaded cells out of 15 total

days.title: Dividing Fractions
days.ncert_reference: NCERT Section 1.1 — division of rational numbers

days.title: Decimals and Rational Form
days.core_concept: Terminating decimals are rational; place-value decomposition
days.ncert_reference: NCERT Section 1.1 — decimal representation of rational numbers

ncert_problem.statement: Express 0.375 in the form p/q, where p and q are integers and q ≠ 0.
steps: Divide numerator and denominator by HCF
Locate on number line between 0 and 1

days.title: Locating Irrational Numbers
days.core_concept: √2 is between 1 and 2; cannot be written as p/q
days.ncert_reference: NCERT Section 1.2 Example 5 — Locate √2 on the number line

ncert_problem.statement: Locate √2 on the number line (construct or mark its approximate position).
steps: Identify that 1² = 1 and 2² = 2, so √2 lies between 1 and 2
Mark the point on the number line between 1 and 2, closer to 1.4
Explain why √2 cannot be expressed as p/q

days.title: Rational vs Irrational — Classification
days.ncert_reference: NCERT Ex 1.2 Q1 — True/false about rational and irrational numbers

ncert_problem.statement: Classify each number as rational or irrational: √4, √5, 22/7, 0.1010010001…
steps: Explain √5 is not a perfect square (irrational)
